headline: Man beaten to death by mob in Dhaka's Jatrabari over mugging suspicion
summary: An unidentified man around 30 years old died at Dhaka Medical College Hospital after being attacked by a crowd at Jatrabari intersection.
details: An unidentified man, aged around 30, died after allegedly being beaten by a mob in Dhaka’s Jatrabari on suspicion of mugging.
The incident occurred near a public toilet at Jatrabari intersection around 3:00 pm, according to police.
Passersby reportedly caught and beat the man after he allegedly snatched a woman’s earring while trying to flee.
The victim was initially taken to Mitford Hospital and later shifted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH), where he died during treatment around 5:45 pm.
Jatrabari Police Station Sub-inspector Md Rafiqul Islam confirmed that the body had multiple injury marks.
Police have informed the CID's forensic team to help establish the man's identity.
Two individuals, including an Ansar member, who transported the man to the hospital have been taken into custody for questioning.

headline_marked: Elephants Samrat and Niharkoli [[returned to Gazipur Safari Park]] after owner breach
headline: Elephants Samrat and Niharkoli returned to Gazipur Safari Park after owner breach
summary: The Forest Department seized two elephants after their owners allegedly failed to comply with release conditions, including bans on torture and extortion.
details: The Forest Department has taken back two elephants, Samrat and Niharkoli, who were returned to their owners on August 12 following a rescue operation.
The animals had previously spent nearly two years at the Gazipur Safari Park after being rescued from owners who allegedly used them to extort money from people on roads and highways.
The elephants were returned to the owners under strict conditions: they must not be tortured or used for extortion and must be properly cared for.
However, authorities acted after reports that Samrat was being used to pull trees in the Lawachhara area and had caused damage to a local shop.
Range officers from Moulvibazar and Sreemangal have secured the animals, and they are currently under the supervision of the Wildlife Management and Nature Conservation Department.
The owners, Monir Mia and Abdul Majid, have denied the allegations, with Monir Mia claiming he had cared for Samrat since he was a calf.
The elephants will now be handed over to safari park officials for their continued care and safety.
